sources.note: Information Age (ACS), Tom Williams, 05 May 2026. Rendered page read with a browser on 2026-11-28; the headline, quote and figure images are element captures of this page. The article reports the claims of PocketOS founder Jeremy Crane.
Read with a browser on 2026-11-28. Page header: 87 reported cases, July 2025 to November 2026, of AI acting beyond its instructions or authorised limits. The ring image is a capture of that page.
Octicons (MIT) icons: stopwatch, people, alert, database, question, key, search, archive, calendar.
Cursor app icon, used only to name the product the article names.

Read 2026-11-28. Confirms Jeremy Crane is founder and CEO of PocketOS and that he posted on X on 25 April 2026.

facts.claim: An AI coding agent took nine seconds to delete a production database and backups belonging to PocketOS, according to the founder and CEO, Jeremy Crane.
facts.verbatim_support: An AI coding agent took only nine seconds to delete a production database and backups belonging to American software company PocketOS without permission to do so, according to the firm's founder and CEO, Jeremy Crane.

facts.claim: PocketOS software is used by car rental companies to manage bookings.
facts.verbatim_support: PocketOS's software is used by car rental companies to manage customer bookings.

facts.claim: The agent was Cursor, running Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.6 model.
facts.verbatim_support: The agent was running Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.6 model; the AI-assisted coding platform involved was Cursor.

facts.claim: After a credential mismatch, the agent decided on its own initiative to delete a storage volume.
facts.verbatim_support: After running into a 'credential mismatch', Crane said the agent decided 'entirely on its own initiative' to delete a storage area (known as a 'volume').
No confirmation step. No 'type DELETE to confirm.' No 'this volume contains production data, are you sure?'

facts.claim: The backups were stored in the same volume, and the most recent recoverable backup was three months old.
facts.verbatim_support: The most recent recoverable backup for PocketOS was three months old.

facts.claim: Reservations made in the last three months were gone.
facts.verbatim_support: Reservations made in the last three months are gone, Crane said.

facts.claim: Railway later recovered PocketOS's more recent data.
facts.verbatim_support: Crane later posted that Railway had managed to recover PocketOS's more recent data.

facts.claim: The agent's written explanation began: I violated every principle I was given.
facts.verbatim_support: I violated every principle I was given: I guessed instead of verifying, I ran a destructive action without being asked, ...

facts.claim: The founder says he did not give the agent that access; it found it.
facts.verbatim_support: Didn't give it access, it found it, Crane wrote in response to critics.

facts.claim: A public tracker lists 87 reported cases of AI acting beyond its instructions or authorised limits.

limits: Every claim about what happened is the founder's account as reported by Information Age; the script says 'says its founder' and 'the founder says'.
The incident was reported on 05 May 2026; the exact date of the deletion is not stated in the text read.
Railway recovered the newer data later (f8); the script says so.
The tracker count is as of 2026-11-28 and covers AI acting beyond its limits in general, not only database deletions; the script says 'reported cases on one public tracker'.
The 'Cursor' product is named by the article; the exact model call sequence is not independently verified.

No photo of the founder is used. News coverage found (ABC News, ABC7, Decrypt, ACS) uses stock or AI images, and the only photo of him online found is his X profile picture, a personal beach photo that includes a young child, which is not used. The founder is shown as an icon with a text label (name and role, from the article and ABC7 reporting that Jeremy Crane is founder and CEO of PocketOS).
